questions.question: What regional brands does the company sell in its international markets?
questions.answer: Pelon Pelo Rico confectionery in Mexico, IO-IO snacks in Brazil, and Sofit beverages in India.
questions.quote: Pelon Pelo Rico confectionery products in Mexico, IO-IO snack products in Brazil, and Sofit beverage products in India

questions.question: What's the downside of raising prices or shrinking pack sizes to cover input cost inflation?
questions.answer: Higher prices or smaller product sizes can reduce sales volume and consumption.
questions.quote: higher product prices or decreased product sizes may also result in a reduction in sales volume and/or consumption

questions.question: What does capturing synergies from the snack acquisitions depend on?
questions.answer: Leveraging Hershey's resources, expertise, capability-building, distribution locations and customer base.
questions.quote: achievement of these synergies will be driven by our ability to successfully leverage Hershey's resources, expertise, capability-building, distribution locations and customer base

questions.question: When did the Lotte Shanghai Foods divestiture close?
questions.answer: January 2021, after a definitive agreement signed in October 2020.
questions.quote: The sale of LSFC was completed in January 2021

questions.question: How did operating margin change in 2020 versus 2019?
questions.answer: Operating profit margin rose to 21.9% in 2020 from 20.0% in 2019.
questions.quote: Operating profit margin | 21.9% | 20.0% | 20.8%

questions.question: Why was ad spending lower in 2020?
questions.answer: Down 2.0% on media cost efficiencies and COVID-related brand investment optimization in International and Other.
questions.quote: Total advertising and related consumer marketing expenses decreased 2.0% driven by media cost efficiencies and select brand investment optimization related to COVID-19 in International and Other segments

questions.question: What drove the increase in diluted EPS in 2020?
questions.answer: Higher gross profit, lower SM&A, lower impairments and lower taxes, plus a lower share count from buybacks.
questions.quote: driven primarily by higher gross profit, lower SM&A, lower impairment charges, and lower income taxes in 2020

questions.question: Why did North America segment income grow in 2020, and what offset it?
questions.answer: Price realization and volume gains, partly offset by COVID-related supply chain costs: PPE, extra sanitation and wage incentives.
questions.quote: primarily due to favorable price realization and volume increases, partially offset by higher supply chain-related costs, specifically, PPE costs, increased sanitation and wage incentives associated with COVID-19

questions.question: Why did operating cash flow decline in 2020?
questions.answer: Working capital used $166M versus generating $60M in 2019, mainly from a bigger U.S. inventory build and higher seasonal receivables.
questions.quote: This $226 million fluctuation was mainly driven by a higher year-over-year build up of U.S. inventories

questions.question: What boosted operating cash flow in 2019?
questions.answer: Working capital swung to a $60M inflow on higher pre-year-end collections, vendor payment timing and higher accrued incentive compensation.
questions.quote: mainly driven by higher cash receipts prior to year-end 2019, the timing of vendor and supplier payments, as well as higher accrued incentive compensation related to annual performance

questions.question: What did Ken Goldman note about this year's advertising spending?
questions.answer: Advertising was pulled back a bit in Q3 and had been up and down this year; he asked about 2021 plans.
questions.quote: you pulled back a little bit on advertising this quarter. It's been a little up and down this year for understandable reasons.

questions.question: How does management plan to set brand investment levels in 2021?
questions.answer: Bring advertising investment back to desired levels, closer to historical norms, after pandemic pullbacks in areas like refreshment.
questions.quote: we definitely plan on taking our investment levels to where we would like them to be and more in line with where they have been historically

questions.question: What is holding back M&A deals right now?
questions.answer: The most attractive targets are riding strong demand and still expect pre-COVID or higher valuations; the funnel stays active.
questions.quote: they still have valuation expectations that look like they did pre-COVID, if not higher

questions.question: What concern did David Palmer raise about U.S. chocolate share gains?
questions.answer: That gains driven by competitors' supply chain breakdowns or poor adaptability might partly reverse in 2021.
questions.quote: if there is a supply chain breakdown or lack of adaptability by a competitor, maybe that will represent share gains that they can reverse somewhat in 21

questions.question: Why does selling through Halloween inventory quickly matter for the holiday season?
questions.answer: It clears shelf space so holiday product can go on the floor, giving holiday a fast start.
questions.quote: it helps us get that fast start to holiday because it clears the space to be able to put holiday on the floor

questions.question: What did Jason English credit for the unusually strong early Halloween selling?
questions.answer: Retailer merchandising programs that started bigger and earlier than usual.
questions.quote: I think a big part of that is due to the merchandising programs that retailers had. It seems like they started bigger and earlier than they usually do.

questions.question: What did Jason English say a mid-single-digit category decline for the full season would imply for upcoming retail data?
questions.answer: Sharp declines would have to show up in retail sales data over the next couple of weeks as the late season is captured.
questions.quote: to get the category down mid-single digits, we're going to have to see some pretty sharp declines coming through the retail sales data in the next couple of weeks

questions.question: What does management expect for promotional spending through Q4 and into 2021?
questions.answer: No significant change; promotions weren't run differently this year and none are expected going forward.
questions.quote: we don't see any significant change relative to promotional activity

questions.question: What new product format is being tested under the Reese's brand?
questions.answer: Reese's snack cakes, launched on a very small scale, with encouraging early test results.
questions.quote: We are on a very small level launching snack cakes under our Reese's trademark

questions.question: What will drive gross margin in 2021?
questions.answer: A mix more driven by volume than price, continued productivity goals, and the 2020 and 2021 cocoa crops.
questions.quote: we'll have a little bit more volume-driven than price-driven mix driving gross margin next year

questions.question: How does the company say it holds its ground against larger rivals?
questions.answer: By successfully designing, developing and marketing complex timing solutions for its customers.
questions.quote: We maintain our competitive position through our ability to successfully design, develop, and market complex timing solutions for the customers we serve.

questions.question: What kind of warranty exposure could cause results to swing?
questions.answer: Significant warranty claims, including ones its suppliers don't cover.
questions.quote: significant warranty claims, including those not covered by our suppliers

questions.question: How could customers' product delays hurt the company's competitiveness?
questions.answer: If customers delay or cancel products designed around its silicon timing solutions, its products could become uncompetitive or obsolete.
questions.quote: the delay or cancellation of any of our customers’ product offerings for which our silicon timing systems solutions are designed

questions.question: How could component shortages at customers affect demand for its products?
questions.answer: If customers or their contract manufacturers can't get enough third-party components used alongside its parts, demand and sales could fall.
questions.quote: the inability of our customers or their contract manufacturers to obtain sufficient supplies of third-party components used with our products could result in a decline in the demand of our products and a loss of sales

questions.question: What dilution risk do shareholders face if the company needs more funding?
questions.answer: Raising money via equity or convertible debt could significantly dilute holders, and new securities may rank senior to common stock.
questions.quote: If we raise additional funds by issuing equity securities or convertible debt, stockholders may experience significant dilution of their ownership interest

questions.question: How large are the federal and state NOL carryforwards?
questions.answer: About $201.5 million federal and $64.0 million state as of December 31, 2020.
questions.quote: U.S. federal and state net operating loss (“NOL”) carryforwards of approximately $201.5 million and $64.0 million, respectively

questions.question: Why might the company see more intellectual property claims going forward?
questions.answer: Its higher profile and visibility as a public company may attract infringement allegations.
questions.quote: particularly as a public company with an increased profile and visibility

questions.question: What natural disaster risk does the company's location create?
questions.answer: Its headquarters and some suppliers and foundry vendors sit in active earthquake zones.
questions.quote: Our corporate headquarters and some of our suppliers and foundry vendors are located in areas that are in active earthquake zones

questions.question: How could pandemic-related credit market stress affect the company's funding?
questions.answer: Tighter credit markets could limit external financing for operations and capex; bank failures could cause losses on cash and investments.
questions.quote: the deterioration in credit markets could limit our ability to obtain external financing to fund our operations and capital expenditures

questions.question: What typically happens to demand, inventory and pricing in a chip industry downturn?
questions.answer: Weaker demand, production overcapacity, high inventories and faster erosion of average selling prices.
questions.quote: Downturns in the semiconductor industry have been characterized by diminished product demand, production overcapacity, high inventory levels, and accelerated erosion of average selling prices.

questions.question: Which parts of the radio network are seeing Open RAN traction for the company?
questions.answer: Worldwide O-RAN traction across radio networks, including RRUs, small cells and distributed units.
questions.quote: We're getting significant traction with O-RAN customers worldwide across the entire radio networks, including RRUs, small cells, and distributed units.

questions.question: What is fourth-quarter revenue guidance?
questions.answer: Up 10% to 15% sequentially, about $36.8 million at the midpoint, roughly 30% above the year-ago quarter.
questions.quote: We expect fourth quarter revenue will be up 10% to 15% sequentially.

questions.question: When did management last raise guidance before reporting Q3, and how did results compare?
questions.answer: Guidance was raised in late August, and Q3 results came in above that updated range.
questions.quote: you updated guidance in late August, positively, and then you're now coming ahead of that range now

questions.question: How many MEMS resonator units can a handful of wafers produce?
questions.answer: About 10 wafers yield roughly a billion units, using 180-nanometer technology.
questions.quote: 10 wafers should give us about a billion units

questions.question: How concentrated is the supply of ceramic packages for quartz timing parts?
questions.answer: Only two suppliers worldwide make them, and shortages sometimes occur.
questions.quote: Those quartz packaging, ceramic packages, come from only two people in the world, and sometimes there's a shortage.

questions.question: How big is the serviceable addressable market?
questions.answer: Around $1.0 to $1.2 billion, mostly oscillators and under $2 billion, within a roughly $8 billion total timing market.
questions.quote: our SAM is still around a billion to a billion point two

questions.question: What did Quinn Bolton ask about mask sets for the new silicon resonators?
questions.answer: Whether a new mask set is needed every time the resonator frequency changes.
questions.quote: do you need new mask sets every time the frequency changes in those resonator structures?

questions.question: Over what time frame does management expect the 5G infrastructure buildout to play out?
questions.answer: Probably a five-to-seven-year rollout, seen as a solid, steady growth area.
questions.quote: this is probably a five, seven-year rollout

questions.question: What process geometries does the company use for its tape-outs?
questions.answer: Mature nodes of 180, 130 and 65 nanometers, unlike peers taping out at 7 nanometers.
questions.quote: we're doing 180, 130, 65 nanometer tape outs

questions.question: When was revenue from the Cascade clock IC expected to begin?
questions.answer: In 2021, then ramping beyond that, per the analyst's recap of last quarter's comments.
questions.quote: you expected revenue to really be a 2021 event beginning and then probably ramping beyond that

questions.question: How were the reporting segments reorganized in 2020?
questions.answer: From Q3 2020, the Middle East moved out of Asia Pacific and Middle East into Europe and North Africa; segments were renamed.
questions.quote: The Middle East business was realigned from the Asia Pacific and Middle East segment to the Europe and North Africa segment.

questions.question: How did Greater Prudhoe Area production change in 2020?
questions.answer: Average net production rose from 81 MBOED in 2019 to 84 MBOED in 2020.
questions.quote: Average net production increased from 81 MBOED in 2019 to 84 MBOED in 2020.

questions.question: How is LNG output contracted and priced?
questions.answer: Mainly under long-term contracts priced off market indices, focused on equity LNG in Australia and Qatar.
questions.quote: LNG is primarily sold under long-term contracts with prices based on market indices.

questions.question: What priorities guided the company's COVID-19 response?
questions.answer: Protecting employees, mitigating the spread of COVID-19 and running the business safely.
questions.quote: to protect our employees, mitigate the spread of COVID-19 and safely run the business

questions.question: How does the company recruit a more diverse workforce?
questions.answer: Inclusive job descriptions, diverse interview panels, and recruiting at conferences, Hispanic-serving institutions and HBCUs.
questions.quote: By attending conferences and recruiting at Hispanic-serving institutions and historically black colleges and universities, we have extended a broader outreach to potential diverse candidates.

questions.question: How could persistently low oil and gas prices affect DD&A expense?
questions.answer: Lower reserve estimates could raise the unit-of-production DD&A rate.
questions.quote: If oil and gas prices persist at depressed levels, our reserve estimates may decrease further, which could incrementally increase the rate used to determine DD&A expense on our unit-of-production method properties.

questions.question: Why are national oil companies a competitive threat?
questions.answer: State-owned rivals may be driven by politics with less focus on financial returns, putting the company at a disadvantage.
questions.quote: we may be at a competitive disadvantage when competing with state-owned companies if they are motivated by political or other factors in making their business decisions, with less emphasis on financial returns

questions.question: Where does the U.S. stand on the Paris climate agreement?
questions.answer: The U.S. had withdrawn, but the new administration recommitted to the agreement.
questions.quote: While the U.S. previously withdrew from the Paris Agreement, the new administration has recommitted the United States to the Paris Agreement

questions.question: How much was the quarterly dividend raised in October 2020?
questions.answer: From $0.42 to $0.43 per share.
questions.quote: increase to our quarterly dividend from $0.42 per share to $0.43 per share

questions.question: How much in extra cost cuts was identified after the Concho deal was announced?
questions.answer: A further $250 million of combined-company cost reductions, to be achieved by 2022.
questions.quote: we identified $250 million of further cost reductions from the combined companies to be achieved by 2022

questions.question: What portion of cash from operations does the company aim to return to shareholders?
questions.answer: More than 30% of CFO annually, a target the Concho deal strengthens.
questions.quote: our stated target of returning more than 30% of our CFO to our owners annually

questions.question: Who is leading the Concho integration on each side?
questions.answer: Dominic Macklon for ConocoPhillips and Will Giroux for Concho.
questions.quote: Dominic Macklin will lead the effort for ConocoPhillips, and Will Giroux will lead the effort for Concha.

questions.question: What should investors use as the starting point for 2021 capital and production?
questions.answer: Fourth-quarter 2020 guidance is the new baseline, subject to ongoing market monitoring.
questions.quote: you should take the fourth quarter as the new baseline for 21 capital and production

questions.question: What pro forma cash flow does the combined company generate at $40 oil?
questions.answer: Roughly $7.5 to $7.8 billion at $40 a barrel, including the full $350 million of cash cost savings.
questions.quote: it would imply somewhere between seven and a half and seven eight at $40 a barrel

questions.question: What marketing synergy does management see from combining with Concho?
questions.answer: Concho sells at the wellhead; ConocoPhillips sells further down the value chain for better realizations.
questions.quote: Concho typically sells their product to the wellhead. We sell further down the value chain to improve realisation.

questions.question: What did Neil Mehta ask about equity affiliate distributions?
questions.answer: How to model distributions, including APLNG, at different oil prices, given the deck said they wouldn't be ratable.
questions.quote: Can you talk about different oil price levels and how we should be thinking about modeling those distributions coming into the business?

questions.question: How much in equity affiliate distributions should be modeled for 2021?
questions.answer: About $600 to $800 million at strip prices, with APLNG weighted to the second and fourth quarters.
questions.quote: if you're thinking of the range of $600 to $800 million from equity affiliates at those kind of pricing, that's going to get you in the ballpark

questions.question: How is the planned Alaska equity sell-down tied to Willow's timing?
questions.answer: It isn't: a sell-down is still expected but slowed, and project timing doesn't depend on it.
questions.quote: the timing of the project isn't contingent on the sell-down

questions.question: When will 2021 capital guidance for the combined company be issued?
questions.answer: Not until sometime after the Concho transaction closes.
questions.quote: you shouldn't expect us to communicate 2021 capital guidance, certainly for the combined company, until sometime after the transaction closes

questions.question: What did Roger Read ask about assets losing exploration and appraisal funding?
questions.answer: Whether those assets go back into the resource base or become more likely to be sold or monetized another way.
questions.quote: Do they just go back into the resource base, or is that something that maybe becomes more likely to be disposed of, you know, monetized in a different way?
